item.title: Xi says China ready to work with Uzbekistan to usher in new "golden decade" for bilateral relations
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
BISHKEK, Aug. 31 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Monday that China stands ready to work with Uzbekistan to usher in a new "golden decade" for bilateral relations, as the two sides celebrate the 10th anniversary of the China-Uzbekistan comprehensive strategic partnership. Xi made the remarks in a meeting with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Summit 2026 in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. Under the leadership of the two heads of state, bilateral relations have continued to improve and upgrade, with fruitful cooperation across various fields and notable progress in building a China-Uzbekistan community with a shared future, Xi said. China stands ready to work with Uzbekistan to consolidate strategic mutual trust and deepen mutually beneficial cooperation, Xi added. Xi stressed that no matter how the international situation changes, China's commitment to deepening bilateral friendship will remain unwavering, and China will continue to support Uzbekistan in pursuing a development path suited to its national conditions.

item.title: Xi, Japarov chart new course for China-Kyrgyzstan ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Aug. 31, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan) * China stands ready to work with Kyrgyzstan to deliver more practical cooperation outcomes that are tangible and accessible, Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Monday during talks with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov. * Xi said that in recent years, China-Kyrgyzstan relations have achieved leapfrog development, boosting the development of both countries and contributing to peace, stability and prosperity in the region. * Xi urged the two countries to deepen practical cooperation, implement the intergovernmental economic and trade cooperation plan, diversify trade products and develop new growth areas. * China and Kyrgyzstan should expand cooperation in law enforcement and security, work together to combat the "three evil forces," drug trafficking and transnational crimes, and jointly maintain regional peace and stability, Xi said. BISHKEK, Aug. 31 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said here on Monday that China stands ready to work with Kyrgyzstan to deliver more practical cooperation outcomes that are tangible and accessible. Xi made the remarks during talks with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov. Xi landed in Bishkek on Sunday for a state visit to Kyrgyzstan and to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026. The visit came as the China-Kyrgyzstan cooperation has ushered in a "golden period" of rapid development, as noted by Xi in a written speech delivered upon his arrival, with the two countries working to translate their longstanding friendship and strong political mutual trust into broader cooperation and greater benefits for their people. Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in Bishkek for the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026 and a state visit to Kyrgyzstan upon the invitation of President Sadyr Japarov of Kyrgyzstan, Aug. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) DEEPENING TRUST, BUILDING A SHARED FUTURE The visit coincides with the 35th anniversary of Kyrgyzstan's independence. On behalf of the Chinese government and people, Xi first extended greetings to Japarov on the occasion of Kyrgyzstan's Independence Day. Xi said that in recent years, China-Kyrgyzstan relations have achieved leapfrog development under the joint guidance of the two leaders, with cooperation across all fields flourishing, boosting the development of both countries and bringing benefits to their people, while also contributing to peace, stability and prosperity in the region. Xi noted that this year marks the 105th anniversary of the founding of the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the launch of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030). China is building a great country in all respects and advancing the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation on all fronts through Chinese modernization, Xi said, noting that Kyrgyzstan is also making every effort to implement its National Development Program until 2030. China stands ready to work with Kyrgyzstan to strengthen the alignment of development strategies, deepen exchanges on governance experience, and make substantive progress in building a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future, he added. Xi noted that high-level political mutual trust and firm mutual support are crucial to ensuring the steady and sustained development of China-Kyrgyzstan relations. China firmly supports Kyrgyzstan in safeguarding its national sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity, as well as pursuing a development path suited to its national conditions, Xi said, adding that China stands ready to work with the Kyrgyz side to continue firmly supporting each other on issues involving each other's core interests. For his part, Japarov said he was honored to welcome Xi to Kyrgyzstan on the occasion of the 35th anniversary of the country's independence. The visit further demonstrated the profound friendship and high-level political mutual trust between Kyrgyzstan and China, and marked an important milestone in the history of bilateral relations, he said. Japarov said Kyrgyzstan and China are neighboring countries, and the ancient Silk Road has closely connected the two nations. In recent years, with the rapid development of the Kyrgyzstan-China comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era, bilateral relations have entered a golden period and reached an unprecedented level, he said. He expressed gratitude to China for its selfless support and assistance at every critical moment in Kyrgyzstan's development, while extending warm congratulations on the 105th anniversary of the founding of the CPC and the launch of the implementation of China's 15th Five-Year Plan. Japarov also expressed admiration for the remarkable development achievements China has made under the leadership of Xi, and voiced willingness to learn from China's experience in state governance, particularly Xi's commitment to the people, as embodied in his words, "I will fully commit to the people and never fail them." China has always been a priority in Kyrgyzstan's foreign policy, as well as Kyrgyzstan's closest friend and most reliable partner, Japarov said, noting that Kyrgyzstan firmly adheres to the one-China principle and stands ready to further develop good-neighborly and friendly relations with China on the basis of mutual respect, equality and mutual benefit. Chinese President Xi Jinping, accompanied by Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov, inspects the guard of honor during a welcome ceremony in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Aug. 31, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Ye) EXPANDING PRACTICAL COOPERATION, DELIVERING TANGIBLE BENEFITS Xi urged the two countries to deepen practical cooperation, effectively implement the intergovernmental economic and trade cooperation plan, diversify trade products and develop new growth areas such as digital trade and cross-border e-commerce. Xi also said the two sides should ensure the high-quality construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, calling it a major transportation artery that carries the development aspirations of the people across the region. He called for modernizing border ports and deepening "soft connectivity" in institutions, standards and rules, and urged the launch of more landmark projects in renewable energy, resource recycling and other fields, the implementation of cooperation documents on green minerals, and cooperation across the entire industrial chain. Xi said China and Kyrgyzstan should make joint efforts to successfully build the Belt and Road Joint Laboratory, enhance artificial intelligence cooperation, and leverage scientific and technological innovation to boost the quality and efficiency of bilateral cooperation. The two sides should further facilitate exchanges and expand cooperation in youth affairs, media, tourism, sports, health care and local affairs, while continuing to strengthen the social and public support for China-Kyrgyzstan friendship, Xi added. For his part, Japarov said Kyrgyzstan is willing to strengthen cooperation with China in trade and investment, connectivity, technological innovation, energy, mineral resources and the green economy, as well as deepen exchanges in education, health, culture and youth sectors. Kyrgyzstan is ready to actively advance the construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, so as to turn it into a "steel Silk Road" for the new era and a new bond of friendship between the two countries, Japarov said. Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Aug. 31, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) JOINING HANDS FOR PEACE AND DEVELOPMENT China and Kyrgyzstan should expand cooperation in law enforcement and security, work together to combat the "three evil forces" of terrorism, extremism and separatism, drug trafficking and transnational crimes, and jointly maintain regional peace and stability, Xi said. China supports Kyrgyzstan in playing a greater role in international and regional affairs, Xi said, noting that China is willing to further enhance collaboration with Kyrgyzstan within the framework of the United Nations, jointly implement the four major global initiatives, oppose hegemonism and power politics, adhere to true multilateralism, safeguard international fairness and justice, and promote the building of a more just and equitable global governance system. Noting that China and Kyrgyzstan are both founding members of the SCO, Xi said the two countries should promote the implementation of the outcomes of the Tianjin Summit, facilitate common development in the region, and advance the development of the SCO to a new level. For his part, Japarov said that the four global initiatives proposed by President Xi help countries work together to address common challenges and build a more just and stable international order. Kyrgyzstan stands ready to closely coordinate with China on multilateral platforms, including the United Nations, the SCO, the China-Central Asia mechanism and the World AI Cooperation Organization, to jointly safeguard world peace and stability, Japarov said. Following the talks, the two heads of state signed a joint declaration of the People's Republic of China and the Kyrgyz Republic on the high-quality development of the comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era and a bilateral treaty on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation. The signing of the bilateral treaty on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation will provide an important legal foundation for the everlasting friendship and firm mutual support between the two countries, Xi said. Echoing Xi, Japarov said the signing of the treaty will open up broader prospects for bilateral relations. They also jointly witnessed the exchange of bilateral cooperation documents in the fields of investment, transportation, customs, and sister-city relations. During the visit, the two sides also signed over 20 cooperation documents covering science and technology, education, culture, media, and other areas.

item.title: Xi expects stronger foundation, brighter future for China-Russia ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
BISHKEK, Aug. 31 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Monday that, under his and Russian President Vladimir Putin's strategic guidance and through the joint efforts of both sides, the foundation of China-Russia relations will become ever stronger, their progress ever steadier, and their future ever brighter. Xi made the remarks in a meeting with Putin on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026 in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. Xi said that during the successful state visit of Putin to China in May, he and Putin made arrangements to steer bilateral relations toward higher-quality and higher-level development from a strategic and long-term perspective, and reached consensus on deepening cooperation between China and Russia across various sectors under the new circumstances. The competent authorities of the two countries are actively implementing the consensus, with substantial results already made, Xi said, adding that exchanges and cooperation between the two sides have maintained a strong momentum. Xi noted that the international landscape is witnessing a notable increase in uncertain and unpredictable factors, against the backdrop of accelerating profound changes unseen in a century. But the pursuit of people across the world of peace, development, cooperation and win-win outcomes remains unchanged, he added. The SCO shoulders the important responsibility for safeguarding regional stability and promoting regional development, he said. China, he said, stands ready to work with Russia and other parties to jointly chart the course for the development of the SCO, help ensure its steady and sustained progress, and strengthen the driving force for reform of global governance and the advancement of an equal and orderly multipolar world.

item.title: China urges Japan to bring perpetrator over Chinese embassy intrusion to account: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
BEIJING, Aug. 31 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese side noted that Japanese public prosecutors have indicted the person concerned in the Chinese embassy intrusion incident, urging the Japanese side to earnestly fulfill its duty and bring the perpetrator to account, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said on Monday. According to media reports, Japan's Self-Defense Forces (SDF) said in a statement on Aug. 28 that they had dismissed SDF officer Kodai Murata, who allegedly scaled a barbed-wire wall and broke into the Chinese embassy in Tokyo with an 18-cm blade on March 24, threatening to kill Chinese diplomatic personnel. Spokesperson Guo Jiakun made the remarks at a daily news briefing when asked for comments, saying that it is shockingly malignant for a sitting Japanese SDF officer to break into the Chinese embassy carrying a knife and threaten the Chinese side with violence. Guo said this incident seriously violates the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, gravely threatens the safety and security of Chinese diplomatic personnel and premises, and exposes deep-seated problems in Japan, including the rampant spread of right-wing impact and lack of supervision and discipline in the SDF. "We urge the Japanese side to earnestly fulfill its duty, bring the perpetrator to account, conduct a thorough investigation and correct the wrongdoings. This is also what the international community hopes to see," said Guo.

item.title: Xi expects stronger foundation, brighter future for China-Russia ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Summit 2026 in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Aug. 31, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BISHKEK, Aug. 31 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Monday that, under his and Russian President Vladimir Putin's strategic guidance and through the joint efforts of both sides, the foundation of China-Russia relations will become ever stronger, their progress ever steadier, and their future ever brighter. Xi made the remarks in a meeting with Putin on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026 in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. Xi said that during the successful state visit of Putin to China in May, he and Putin made arrangements to steer bilateral relations toward higher-quality and higher-level development from a strategic and long-term perspective, and reached consensus on deepening cooperation between China and Russia across various sectors under the new circumstances. The competent authorities of the two countries are actively implementing the consensus, with substantial results already made, Xi said, adding that exchanges and cooperation between the two sides have maintained a strong momentum. Xi noted that the international landscape is witnessing a notable increase in uncertain and unpredictable factors, against the backdrop of accelerating profound changes unseen in a century. But the pursuit of people across the world of peace, development, cooperation and win-win outcomes remains unchanged, he added. The SCO shoulders the important responsibility for safeguarding regional stability and promoting regional development, he said. China, he said, stands ready to work with Russia and other parties to jointly chart the course for the development of the SCO, help ensure its steady and sustained progress, and strengthen the driving force for reform of global governance and the advancement of an equal and orderly multipolar world. Amid a turbulent and complex international landscape, Russia and China have continuously deepened their comprehensive strategic coordination, upholding equality, mutual trust, and mutual support, while cooperation and development across various fields have advanced rapidly, and Russia-China relations have become a model for relations between countries, Putin said. Russia is willing to maintain high-level exchanges with China, strengthen cooperation in areas such as trade, energy, industry, transportation, and science and technology, enhance people-to-people and cultural exchanges, and promote bilateral relations to achieve new results, he said. Through the joint efforts of all parties, the SCO has evolved into a dynamic and efficient regional cooperation platform with significant international influence, said Putin, noting that Russia and China should continuously strengthen their solidarity and cooperation within the organization and play a guiding role. Russia is willing to strengthen coordination and cooperation with China within multilateral mechanisms such as the United Nations, the BRICS mechanism and the G20, support China in hosting the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, and jointly uphold world peace, stability and prosperity, he said. The two heads of state also exchanged views on international and regional issues of common concern. item.title: Xi says China-Kyrgyzstan cooperation entering "golden period" of rapid development
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-30
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan step out of the airplane cabin upon arrival in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Aug. 30, 2026. Xi landed in Bishkek on Sunday for the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026 and a state visit to Kyrgyzstan upon the invitation of President Sadyr Japarov of Kyrgyzstan. (Xinhua/Zhai Jianlan) BISHKEK, Aug. 30 (Xinhua) -- The China-Kyrgyzstan cooperation has ushered in a "golden period" of rapid development, Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Sunday as he landed here for the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026 and a state visit to Kyrgyzstan. Upon the arrival, Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and his wife welcomed Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, at the Manas International Airport. In a written speech, Xi extended sincere greetings and best wishes to Japarov and the people of Kyrgyzstan on behalf of the Chinese government and people. Noting that China and Kyrgyzstan share a time-honored traditional friendship, Xi said that the majestic Tianshan Mountains stands as witnesses to the millennia of friendly exchanges between their peoples. Over the 34 years since the establishment of diplomatic relations, the China-Kyrgyzstan relationship has withstood the test of a changing international landscape, maintained sound and stable development throughout, and reached the high level of a comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era. In recent years, bilateral trade volume and people-to-people exchanges have reached new highs, Xi said, noting that major projects including the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway have been successfully implemented, and the tangible results of mutually beneficial cooperation have broadly benefited the two peoples. Xi said that during the visit he will have in-depth exchanges of views with Japarov on China-Kyrgyzstan relations, cooperation in various fields between the two countries, and international and regional issues of common concern, and draw a new blueprint for building a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future. "I look forward to attending the SCO Bishkek Summit, working with all parties to revisit the 25-year development experience of the SCO, jointly discuss cooperation plans, create the future of the organization, and promote the continuous new development of the organization," Xi said.

item.title: China urges Japan to accelerate disposal of abandoned chemical weapons
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
Gas masks produced by the Japanese military in China during WWII are displayed at the Museum of the Imperial Palace of Manchukuo, Changchun City, northeast China's Jilin Province, February 27, 2025. /VCG China on Friday urged the Japanese government to speed up the disposal of abandoned chemical weapons left in China from World War II. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian made the remarks at a regular press briefing in response to a question about a recent exhibition on Japanese military poison gas held by a civil group in Yokohama, Japan. The exhibition showcased how the Japanese military produced poison gas and chemical weapons during World War II and used them in China and other Southeast Asian countries. Lin said Japanese militarism openly violated international law during World War II by developing chemical weapons on a large scale and using them in China and other Asian countries, bringing severe suffering and disasters to people across the region. Equipment used by the Japanese military to produce chemical weapons in China is displayed at the Museum of the Imperial Palace of Manchukuo, February 27, 2025. /VCG "After its defeat, Japan left behind a large number of chemical weapons in China in an attempt to cover up its crimes," Lin said, adding that these abandoned weapons have caused casualties among more than 2,000 people to date and posed serious threats to people's lives, safety and the ecological environment in China. Lin urged the Japanese government to fulfill its obligations, heed calls from Japanese people with a sense of justice and neighboring countries that suffered from the wartime atrocities, and fully and faithfully implement the relevant international conventions and the memorandum between the Chinese and Japanese governments. He called on Japan to accelerate the disposal process of abandoned chemical weapons and return a safe and clean environment to the Chinese people at an early date.
